overview: This 276-page file traces U.S. and Argentine investigations of suspected Japanese espionage and propaganda in Argentina during and after World War II. FBI reports, diplomatic correspondence, Argentine police proceedings, and interrogations examine embassy contacts, couriers, businesses, shipping, and community organizations. Many allegations remained unsubstantiated; later records document the restoration of Japanese associations and relief work.
interest: The file pairs detailed surveillance and police testimony with later interrogations, revealing both intelligence networks and the limits of wartime allegations.
